Small Causes Judge & Acjm,
 Court of Small Causes,
 Member, Mact-12, Bengaluru.

Dated this the 8th day of January, 2025
 MVC.No.3664/2023

Petitioner : Poornima.R  D/o Ramareddy  Aged about 31 years  R/at Gangavara, Doddigere Post,
 Devanahalli Taluk, Bangalore Rural.

(By Sri. C.Giri Babu, Advocate)
 V/
s Respondent/s: The Managing Director
BMTC Central Office  Shanthinagar, K.H.Road  Bangalore-560027.

(Insurer of BMTC Bus bearing  Reg.No.KA-57-F-1195)
 (R1 - By Sri. Jagadeesh.G.S,
 Advocate)
JUDGMENT
This petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of M.V.Act, 1989 claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- in respect of accidental injuries sustained by her in the Road Traffic Accident.

2. In the petition it is stated that on 18.04.2023 at about 6.15 pm petitioner was proceeding in motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-HQ-2337 slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules and when she came near Sundaram Motors, Hoodi main road, at that time the driver of one BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-1195 drove the same in rash and negligent manner with high speed and suddenly turned his bus towards right side and dashed to the motor cycle and thereby caused accident
as a result petitioner fell down from the motor cycle and sustained severe injuries to her legs, hands and all over the body.

She was immediately shifted to MTB hospital, Bangalore and thereafter shifted to Srinivasa hospital, Hoskote and later she was admitted to RxDx hospital,
Poornima.R vs B.M.T.C on 8 January, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24213177/
1 Bangalore wherein she was treated as inpatient for 2 days.
Petitioner was treated surgically and also took followup treatment.
She has spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the date of accident, she was hale and healthy working as HR in Indiqsoft Solutions and earning Rs.32,000/- per month and contributing her entire salary to the family.
Due to injuries sustained by her she is lot of pain and agony.
The jurisdictional Mahadevapura Traffic police have registered a case in Crime No.54/2023 against the driver of aforesaid BMTC (SCCH-12) 3 MVC.No.3664/2023 Bus.

That after the accident, driver of BMTC bus has paid Rs.8,000/- by phone pay and agreed to pay entire hospital expenses and has requested not to lodge complaint against him, but the driver failed to do so as agreed by him and hence there was delay in lodging complaint.
On the date of accident respondent is owner and said bus was covered under internal insurance.
Hence respondent is solely liable to pay compensation.
On all these grounds she prayed to allow the petition and award compensation along with interest and costs in the above case.
3. On issuance of notice to the respondent is served.

He appeared through his counsel and filed detailed written statement and contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is neither maintainable in law nor on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
That as per information and details received by this respondent, there is no negligence on the part of the driver fo the bus bearing No.KA-57-F-1195.
On the contrary petitioner was responsible for the alleged accident since petitioner was riding the motor cycle bearing No.KA-53- HQ-2337 and due to her own negligence the accident took place.
The petitioner has filed the above petition on the basis of assumptions and presumption and same is speculative in nature.

That the driver of the aforesaid bus was on his duty and driver the said bus at route No.VTE07 from Tata Alaxi Bus stop to Kattriguppe Bus stop and when he reached Hoodi main road at that time, the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-53- HQ-2337 came in rash and negligent manner and without (SCCH-12) 4 MVC.No.3664/2023 observing taking 'U' turn dashed to the right side of the bus and the rider of motor cycle and pillion rider fell on the road.
Thus there was no negligence on the part of driver of BMTC bus.
That the rider of aforesaid motorcycle was not qualified rider and she was not possessing valid driving license at the time of accident.
That on the date of accident, the driver of the bus on humanitarian ground paid Rs.8,000/- to the petitioner for medical treatment as full and final settlement.
Manner of accident alleged in the petition is denied.
The age, occupation and income alleged by the petitioner are denied.
The compensation claimed and injuries alleged by the petitioner are denied.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, I have framed the following:-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 18.04.2023 at about 6.15 PM she was proceeding on motor cycle bearing No.KA-53-HQ-2337 on Hoodi main road, near Sundaram Motors by following traffic rules, at that time, one BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-1195 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner and caused accident and petitioner sustained grievous injuries as alleged?
Poornima.R vs B.M.T.C on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24213177/
2 2.
Whether the petitioner proves her age, occupation, income and permanent disability if any?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so by whom and what is the quantum?
4. What Order or Award?
5. To prove her case, petitioner is examined as P.W.1.
Ex.P.1 to P.23 documents are marked on his behalf.
On the other hand, driver of respondent is examined as R.W.1 and got marked Ex. R1 to R 3 documents.
He is cross examined and respondent evidence is closed.

6. Heard learned counsel for both sides and perused records.
7.

On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and on hearing arguments, my answers to the above issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.3:
Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.4: As per final order, for the following;
REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1: To prove the averments made in the petition, petitioner entered into the witness box and got examined as P.W.1.
She has reiterated petition averments in her chief examination.

She has produced FIR, copy of complaint, spot panchanama,
police intimation, rough sketch, IMV notice and answer to it, IMV report, wound certificate, final report and discharge summaries at Ex.P.1 to 13.

On perusal of those documents it can be seen that one Srinidhi G. has given police complaint to Mahadevapura police stating that herself and one Poornima the petitioner herein are working at Indiqsoft Solutions at Kundalahalli gate, Bengaluru and on 18.04.2023 (SCCH-12) 6 MVC.No.3664/2023 this first informant was sitting as pillion rider and petitioner was riding the motor cycle bearing No.KA-53-HQ-2337 and coming towards Hoodi junction from Y-Junction at that time, one Volvo BMTC bus bearing reg.No.KA-57-F-1195 came in rash and negligent manner the driver took sudden right turn and dashed to the two wheeler due to which, two wheeler got damaged,
petitioner and pillion rider sustained grievous injuries.
That this first informant and the driver of bus took petitioner to MTB hospital and the driver paid Rs.8,000/- by phone pay for medical expenses.
It is also stated in the first information that driver agreed to pay further medical expenses and took the bus.

Thereafter, petitioner got Poornima.R vs B.M.T.C on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24213177/
3
further treatment on 21.04.2023, 30.04.2023,05.05.2023 and on 10.05.2023 in different hospitals.
When the bus driver was called to pay the medical expenses of those treatment, he stated that he cannot give money and petitioner can file case if she wants.

Therefore, there is delay in filing the complaint and the driver of the BMTC bus was rash and negligent in driving the bus, as such action may be taken against him.
9.

On the basis of this first information received by Mahadevapura police Crime No.54/2023 is registered against the driver of BMTC bus No.KA-57-F-1195 for the offence p/u/s 279, 337 of IPC and Sec.187, 134(B) of IMV Act.
Police intimation is sent in respect of MLC case by MTB hospital stating that Poornima sustained injuries in the road traffic accident on 18.04.2023 at 6.15 pm by BMTC bus.
The spot panchanama shows that the road was one way, having metro (SCCH-12) 7 MVC.No.3664/2023 line in between the road having center median also.
It is main road, straight way having 30ft width the sketch produced at Ex.P.5 shows petitioner was coming in the straight direction and bus was taking right side 'U' turn.
Bus hit the scooter and on the left side of the scooter there was damage.
Left leg of the petitioner got injured.
There is no fresh damage to bus but scooter sustained damage on the left side.
The driver has not given police complaint in respect of negligence of petitioner in riding the two wheeler.
Wound certificate shows that, petitioner sustained laceration of left leg with blunt injury at left leg and left thigh.
As per the final report driver of the bus found to be negligent and charge sheet is filed against him.
10. The said driver appeared before the court and got examined as R.W.1.
He has produced judgment in C.C.No.22536/2023 dt.22.10.2024 in which he was acquitted having prosecution failed to prove the guilt of him in causing the accident.
He contended that since there is judgment of acquittal in his favour, he is not liable to pay any compensation to petitioner.
It is necessary to notice that decree of proof in criminal case is different from the proof of case before the MACT.
That apart, the Tribunal has to assess the case before it independently apart from the the criminal case documents.
In the present case, only on the basis of Ex.R.2 judgment in criminal case in which accused got acquitted.
It cannot be held that he was not rash and negligent in driving the bus.
P.W.1 in her chief examination stated that the driver of the bus was negligent.
One rough sketch prepared by ARTO, BMTC (SCCH-12) 8 MVC.No.3664/2023 Shantinagar is confronted to her and suggestion is made that bus was taking 'U' turn as shown in the sketch.

Sh admitted that bus was taking 'U'
turn and admitted that part of the sketch.
Therefore, the said sketch is marked as Ex.R.1.
In the cross examination of P.W.1 she stated that she had to take 'U' turn and denied the suggestion that herself and bus both were going in the same direction.
She stated that she has seen bus taking 'U' turn and admitted front side of the scooter got damaged.
She admitted bus driver paid Rs.8,000/-.
In the evidence of R.W.1 he contended that, petitioner herself dashed to the bus from behind.

It is necessary to notice that there is no document available on record or oral evidence of independent Poornima.R vs B.M.T.C on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24213177/
4 witness who has seen the accident to show that petitioner was negligent in riding the two wheeler.
Driver of the bus has not made any effort to file case against the petitioner if she has negligently hit the bus.
The suggestion that both the bus and petitioner was traveling in the same direction was denied .
Therefore, sketch produced at Ex.R.1 will not prove the case of respondent.
Therefore in the opinion of this court petitioner has proved that the driver of the bus was rash and negligent in driving the bus.
Accordingly I answer this issue in the Affirmative.
11. ISSUE NO.2 :
In respect of age, petitioner produced her aadhaar card, D.L and Pan card at Ex.P.14 to 16 which shows that she was born on 31.08.1992.
Accident took place on 18.04.2023.
Respondent has disputed the age of the petitioner but there is no contrary document to disbelieve the age (SCCH-12) 9 MVC.No.3664/2023 mentioned in the Ex.P.14 to 16.
Hence the age of petitioner is considered as 30 years at the time of accident.
12. In respect of occupation and income it is stated that, petitioner was working as HR in Indiqsoft Solutions and she was earning Rs.32,000/- per month.
To prove this fact she has produced account statement at Ex.P.24 but there is no evidence of employer to show her actual income as on the date of accident and no salary slip is also produced.
Therefore in the opinion of this court only on the basis of account statement it cannot be held that petitioner was drawing salary of Rs.32,000/- per month.
In that view of the matter notional income has to be considered to decide the compensation.

Accident being taken place in 2023 notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/-
per month.
In respect of permanent disability no doctor evidence is given.
Hence, it is held that petitioner has no permanent disability affecting her income.
Accordingly, I answer this issue Partly in the Affirmative.
13. ISSUE NO.3 :
In view of above reasons, injuries sustained by petitioner are due to the accident caused by the driver of the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-1193.
There is nexus between the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the accident.
Hence she is entitled to compensation at the hands of respondent.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under:
(I) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.17.

Totally she has paid amount of Rs.1,49,599/-
as per Ex.P.17 medical bills.
Petitioner admitted driver has paid (SCCH-12) 10 MVC.No.3664/2023 Rs.8,000/- medical expenses.
Same has to be deducted from medical bills.
Though the bills are disputed, no satisfactory material is placed to disbelieve the bills.
They are supported by prescriptions of the doctor.
Therefore, petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.1,41,599/-.
(ii) Food and nourishment:
The petitioner was admitted in RxDx Hospital, Bengaluru and 2 discharge summaries are produced at Ex.P12 and 13.
She was in hospital for 4 days.
Accident took place in the year 2023.
Since she was in hospital, food and nourishment charges will have to be awarded.
Considering the cost of living, and food, nourishment charges if per day Rs.500/- is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for food and nourishment Rs.500/- x 4 days = Rs.
Poornima

. R vs B.M.T.C on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24213177/
5 2,000/-is awarded.
(iii) Attendant charges:
For a period of inpatient for 4 days some one should have looked after petitioner in the hospital.
Even if her family member has taken care of her in the said period, that family member's income for those days is lost.
Hence per day if Rs.500/- is awarded as attendant charges in 2023, it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for attendant charges Rs.500/- x 4 days =Rs.2,000/-is awarded.
(iv) Loss of income during laid up period:
As per the finding to issue No.2, the income of the petitioner per month is.
She suffered laceration over left leg with blunt injury to thigh region which are grievous in nature.
She was inpatient for 4 days and she was advised to take rest.
Minimum One month is required to recover from such grievous injury.

Therefore, laid up period of petitioner is considered as total One month including in patient period and loss of income during laid up period is Rs.16,000/-x 1=
16,000/-
She is entitled to Rs.16,000/- as loss of income during laid up period.
(v) Conveyance charges:
It is stated that petitioner was shifted to various Hospital and also took follow up treatment.
She has produced travel services bills at Ex.P.18 which is disputed by the respondent.
In those bills Bill No.1 to 5 are not signed by the issuing authority i.e., travel service.
Bill No.6 and 7 are issued by Bengaluru International Airport Taxi Service in which petitioner travel to Whitefield RxDx hospital on 13.06.2023, but on that day there is no medical bill.
Therefore, those bills cannot be considered.
The bill No.8 to 13 are computerized bills which are not supported by Section 65 B Evidence Act Certificate therefore, they also cannot be relied.

However, petitioner has taken treatment at different hospitals and conveyance has to be awarded and in the opinion of this court if the compensation of Rs.5,000/- is awarded under the head of conveyance interest of justice would be met.
Accordingly, conveyance charges of Rs.5,000/- is awarded.
(vi) Loss of future income due to Disability :
As per the findings given to issue no.2, there is no functional disability of the petitioner affecting her income.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under this head.
(vii) For Future medical expenses: There is no evidence in this case to show there is necessity of future medical treatment (SCCH-12) 12 MVC.No.3664/2023 to the petitioner.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under this head.
(viii) For Pain and sufferings:
The petitioner has sustained one grievous injury.
The records show that she underwent continuous treatment.
She was in hospital for 4 days and suffered pain and agony.
Therefore, for pain and suffering the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- .

(ix) Physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life : As per the photographs supported by C.D produced by the petitioner she has ugly scar mark on the left leg and also her evidence says she suffers discomfort.
Certainly accident has caused physical discomfort and came in the way of normal enjoyment of life of petitioner.

Hence in the opinion of this court, petitioner is entitled to Poornima.R vs B.M.T.C on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24213177/
6 compensation under the head of physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under the said head he is entitled for Rs.20,000/-.
(x) Loss of future prospect:

As per the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme court, even in injury cases,
loss of future prospect has to be considered.
But in the present case, the on going through the evidence of assessed doctor and the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner there is no chance of loss of future prospect.
Hence no compensation is awarded under this head.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:-
Sl

. No Particulars of Heads In Rs.
i. Medical expenses 1,41,599/-

ii. Food and nourishment 2,000/-
iii. Attendant charges 2,000/-
iv. Loss of income during laid up 16,000/-
 period v.

Conveyance charges 5,000/-
vi Loss of income due to disability NIL  vii Future medical expenses NIL viii. Pain & Sufferings 20,000/-
ix. Physical discomfort and loss of 20,000/-
 amenities of life x. Loss of future prospect NIL
Therefore, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.2,06,599/- in respect of injuries sustained by her in the Road traffic accident.
Accordingly, I answer this Issue "Partly in Affirmative".
14. ISSUE NO.4:-
In view of above reasons petitioner is entitled to compensation from the hands of Respondent.

Since respondent admitted the insurance policy valid as on the date of accident, he is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner to the tune of Rs.2,06,599/- with interest @ of 6% from the date of petition till the date of payment.

sentences.text: The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,06,599/- with interest @ 6% pa on the said amount from the date of petition till the date of payment.
The respondent is liable to pay the compensation and hereby directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within 2 months from the date of this order.
After such deposit petitioner is entitled to have release of entire compensation.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.

The respondent is liable to pay the compensation and hereby directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within 2 months from the date of this order.
After such deposit petitioner is entitled to have release of entire compensation.

Award be drawn accordingly.

Therefore, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.2,06,599/- in respect of injuries sustained by her in the Road traffic accident.
Accordingly, I answer this Issue "Partly in Affirmative".
In view of above reasons petitioner is entitled to compensation from the hands of Respondent.

Since respondent admitted the insurance policy valid as on the date of accident, he is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner to the tune of Rs.2,06,599/- with interest @ of 6% from the date of petition till the date of payment.
